data.hypothesis: Fusing absolute value into the first reduction removes the full-size temporary pass and its associated initialization. Choosing roughly one partial per 4096 input values, capped at 8192, should expose more CTAs for large inputs while keeping finalization to one CTA with at most 8192 partials; the controller must measure full-call time and validate the FP64 error bound.
data.notes: The baseline is correct with a measured mean of 1.228093878 ms over three samples. This candidate has not been measured; no speedup or error-bound result is claimed. Each launched first-stage CTA writes one partial, and the finalizer consumes exactly those partials and overwrites the output.
transformations: Fuse fabsf(x[i]) into first-stage accumulation, eliminating the intermediate full-size absolute-value array.
Partition input into contiguous CTA chunks sized by ceil(n/partial_count), with partial_count=ceil(n/4096) clamped to [1,8192].
Reduce each CTA's scalar loads with CUB BlockReduce and write one current-call partial per CTA.
Use one final CTA to reduce all partials and overwrite output without atomics or a separate output initialization.
